verdict_reason: No trust-all, no hostname-verification bypass, no insecure fallback and no global javax.net.ssl mutation - the CDP CA is correctly ADDED alongside the default JVM trust store - but an unparseable configured certificate silently degrades to default-only trust instead of failing fast, and the success log misreports the certificate count; the PR's own diff for this file is only the package rename.

todos.issue: cert == null conflates 'no CDP cert configured' with 'cert configured but unparseable' (CertificateLoader.loadCustomCertificate swallows CertificateException and returns null), so a corrupt TRUSTSTORE_CDP_ROOT_CA boots successfully with the default JVM trust store only and fails later at Mongo/CDP TLS connect time instead of at startup
todos.fix: Make CertificateLoader rethrow (e.g. IllegalStateException) when the cdp.certificate property is non-empty but fails to parse, or have it return an Optional plus a 'configured' flag so customSslContext() can fail fast; keep the silent path only for the genuinely-unset case

todos.issue: log.info hardcodes 'initialized successfully with 1 custom certificate' on every path, including when createCombinedTrustManager returned the default-only trust manager because cert was null - operations see '1 custom certificate' precisely when zero were loaded, masking the degradation above
todos.fix: Log the real outcome, e.g. move the message inside the branches or log 'custom certificates loaded: {}' with (cert == null ? 0 : 1)

todos.issue: @Order(Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE) plus the class javadoc claim that it 'ensures the SSLContext is available before other beans (like MongoClient) are created' is untrue - @Order on a @Configuration class affects configuration-class ordering, not bean instantiation timing; ordering here is actually guaranteed by MongoConfig injecting TrustStoreConfiguration
todos.fix: Drop the @Order annotation and the Ordered import, and correct the javadoc to say ordering comes from dependency injection

todos.issue: CombinedTrustManager.checkServerTrusted/checkClientTrusted discard the default trust manager's CertificateException when falling through to the custom trust manager, so when both reject a chain only the custom CDP trust manager's (usually less informative) error surfaces and the real public-CA failure reason is lost
todos.fix: Capture the first exception and attach it via addSuppressed on the exception thrown by the custom trust manager (or log it at debug) before rethrowing

todos.issue: createCombinedTrustManager declares 'throws Exception' and customSslContext catches bare Exception, which trips Sonar java:S112 and also swallows unrelated runtime faults (NPE, bean-wiring errors) behind the misleading 'Cannot initialize SSL context' message
todos.fix: Narrow to 'throws GeneralSecurityException, IOException' on the helper and catch the same specific types in customSslContext
